exactPrompt:
Create one finished opaque landscape pixel-art background for a WWII Yugoslavia artillery/tank game. The two supplied project images are STYLE AND FRAMING references, not edit targets. Match their crisp pixel clusters, restrained natural colors, damaged period masonry, atmospheric distance and low side-view combat strip; do not make a smooth photograph or a flat geometric placeholder. Aim for a landscape canvas around 3:2; keep the actual delivered dimensions and never crop away landmarks to force a size. Make the far edge of a wide, level, dry foreground combat strip a perfectly horizontal line around 80.6 percent of image height. Keep the lower foreground and the band immediately above that line quiet, fairly light and low in small details across the entire width, so dark soldiers, cannons and tanks remain readable anywhere along it. Put distinctive landmarks and sharp grouped details in the middle distance, inside the central 80 percent of the canvas. Leave the upper corners and bottom corners visually calm for existing game overlays. Water, cliffs, trenches, wire and rubble remain BEHIND the playable foreground, never crossing the combat strip. Show clear WWII war damage in the middle distance, appropriate to this location. No people, playable vehicles, labels, text, UI, logos or borders. No modern buildings, memorial complexes, highways, powerlines, tourist platforms or modern bridges. NO painted flames, smoke plumes, sparks or glowing fires anywhere: draw cold charred damage instead; game code will animate effects later. This is a landscape homage with compressed geography, not a claim of a documented battle or tank deployment at this exact viewpoint. Preserve location-specific recognizable forms from the historical notes.
LOCATION: An intimate rolling Kozara woodland landscape: linked rounded forest ridges, descending wooded spurs, patches of deciduous and conifer trees and a small stream valley. Keep its lower rounded silhouette clearly distinct from Sutjeska's high rocky summit and deep mountain canyon. A roofless village outbuilding, snapped trunks and an abandoned earth-and-timber position make the war damage visible. No Mrakovica cylindrical monument, memorial stairs, museum or modern hotel. Open horizontal light dry-earth clearing across the foreground; no foreground trunks hiding units.
Images 1 and 2 establish the exact project pixel style, muted natural olive/ochre/blue-grey palette and flat quiet combat foreground. Image 3 is the real Kozara forest relief: use its linked rounded wooded spurs and alternating broadleaf/conifer stands, not the modern roads or buildings. Make this unmistakably LOWER ROUNDED FOREST HILLS, without an exposed alpine summit, deep rock canyon, cliff wall, cave, citadel or urban town. A layered green wooded ridge fills the middle distance, with a shallow stream valley visible in a gap between trees. In the right middle ground a low timber-and-plaster farm outbuilding has lost most of its tiled roof, showing cold blackened rafters; several splintered tree trunks and an abandoned earth-and-log position left of center show the war. Keep trunks and dense dark trees well above the unit strip. A pale sunlit open clearing occupies the foreground, flat and uninterrupted across full width; from about 73% image height downward keep it quiet enough for small dark units. Its far ground edge near y=825 on a 1024-high canvas is straight and horizontal, a restrained grass/earth boundary rather than an urban masonry curb. No snow, skiers, tourist paths, buildings of the memorial, painted smoke or flames. Preferred opaque 1536x1024 landscape.
